codex: Every part is edible — leaves, flowers, roots. Bitter means nutritious. The first green of spring and the last of fall.
lookalikeNote: Unmistakable once flowering. Young rosette leaves are the safest stage.
name: Dandelion
preparation: Eat raw; boil to reduce bitterness. Roots can be roasted.
sources: Field validation pending — conservative well-known species
description: a plant with jagged leaves and a yellow flower

knowledgeLevels.1: Name: Dandelion. You grab the whole plant.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: roots (roast like coffee), leaves (salad), petals (tea). Selective harvest yields more.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: vitamin C (prevents scurvy), diuretic, liver support. Eating gives +5 health.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: roots best roasted, leaves best young, petals for wine. 2x yield when prepared right.

codex: The survivalist's supermarket: shoots, roots, pollen, and fluff for tinder. If you find cattails, you found water too.
lookalikeNote: Distinctive brown hot-dog head is unmistakable. Harvest shoots before the head forms.
name: Cattail
preparation: Peel young shoots, eat raw or boiled. Roots pounded for starch.
sources: Field validation pending — conservative well-known species
description: tall reeds with brown sausage-shaped heads

knowledgeLevels.1: Name: Cattail. The brown sausage heads.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: high starch, good calories. Rhizomes are survival food.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: harvest rhizomes in fall, shoots in spring. Process for max calories.

codex: Thorns guard the sweetest calories in the woods. Summer's paycheck — eat fresh, dry what you can't carry.
name: Blackberry
preparation: Eat raw. Leaves make a serviceable tea.
sources: Field validation pending — conservative well-known species
description: a thorny bush with dark berries

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: you learn which parts of blackberry are usable.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: nutritional and medicinal properties of blackberry.

codex: Fall's candy. The fruit sweetens after frost — nature's own ripening timer. Dries well for winter stores.
lookalikeNote: Wait for the frost-softened fruit. If it puckers your mouth inside out, it wasn't ready.
name: American Persimmon
preparation: Eat only fully ripe (soft, wrinkled). Unripe = mouthful of chalk.
sources: Field validation pending — conservative well-known species
description: a tree with orange fruit, soft when ripe

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: you learn which parts of american persimmon are usable.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: nutritional and medicinal properties of american persimmon.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: optimal preparation of american persimmon.

codex: Calorie-dense and they keep for months. The woods' savings account — gather in fall, eat all winter.
name: Hickory Nuts
preparation: Crack and pick. Shagbark hickory is the sweet one.
sources: Field validation pending — conservative well-known species

codex: The staple that fed nations. Tannins must be leached or they'll punish you — but leached acorn meal is flour. Flour is bread. Bread is winter.
lookalikeNote: Stick to white oak group (rounded lobe tips). Red oak acorns need far more leaching.
name: White Oak Acorns
preparation: MUST leach: shell, grind, soak in running water until bitterness is gone. White oak group is mildest.
sources: Field validation pending — conservative well-known species
description: a tree with lobed leaves and acorns

knowledgeLevels.1: Name: White Oak Acorns. Basic identification.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: you learn which parts of white oak acorns are usable.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: nutritional and medicinal properties of white oak acorns.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: optimal preparation of white oak acorns.

codex: Flavor is survival too — morale matters. The smell test is the only ID that counts: onion smell or it stays in the ground.
lookalikeNote: CRITICAL: must smell of onion/garlic. No smell = not an onion = do not eat. This rule has no exceptions.
name: Wild Onion
preparation: Eat raw or cooked. The smell test is law.
sources: Field validation pending — conservative well-known species
